correctness.rationale: The unitary map x_n→r^((n−1)/2)x_n gives exactly A_t=D(I−tS)^−1. For each polynomial P, the finite-band singular counting limit is obtained by finite geometric blocks, rank-B circulant perturbations, and two cutoffs; discarded head has rank O(delta/lambda), tail has norm O(lambda/M). Singular-value comparisons and Darboux sums give lambda N(lambda;DP(S))→mean|P|. The geometric series truncation has error E_B with s_n(E_B)≤t^(B+1)/((1−t)n); Ky-Fan counting inequalities and B→∞ give lambda N(lambda;A_t)→mean|(1−te^{i theta})^−1|. Monotone inversion establishes n s_n→c>0. Schatten, logarithmic mean, and strict c>1 follow. Numerical code independently corroborates finite sections only. The proof does not need or assume numerical convergence implies an infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Exact same-object Rhaly 1982/1984 primary papers, the 2015 weighted-space article, and finite Toeplitz singular-distribution theory were compared at statement/implication level. They provide compactness, eigenvalues, Hilbert–Schmidt norm, weighted norm/spectral analyses or finite Toeplitz distribution but no located direct infinite geometric-weight singular asymptotic. The transfer to an infinite compact operator with 1/n diagonal is established rather than assumed. The main remaining originality risk is equivalence to a general discrete pseudodifferential Weyl theorem or material obscured in the inaccessible typeset source.
residual_risks: Earlier general singular-number Weyl theorems for half-line discrete pseudodifferential or diagonal-times-Toeplitz operators might subsume this concrete coefficient without mentioning Cesàro.
The full typeset 2015 weighted-space article was not available by the tried authorized PDF channels; material text extraction is partly garbled and could hide a relevant formula.
No negative database search establishes global mathematical novelty; unpublished overlapping work is inaccessible.

value.rationale: The generalized Cesàro family is a longstanding natural compact nonnormal operator family studied since 1982; sharp ordered-singular asymptotics were not among the inspected invariants. One exact function c(r) classifies its first-order approximation-number profile for every 0<r<1, determines the sharp weak-trace-class/Dixmier logarithmic coefficient and entire Schatten threshold, and quantifies a strict gap from the known eigenvalue coefficient 1. This is structural asymptotic information, not an arbitrary finite slice or a restatement of compactness. The proof also isolates a reusable finite-band localization argument.
